verdict: Recovery was reliable, but orchestration after recovery was not lean. A preventable startup stop cost 5h29m51s, and the resumed run then concentrated nearly eleven hours in a serial common-runtime review loop without starting either task-specific implementation lane.

evidence: The root waited 3m29.7s for hook-trust confirmation before starting writers.
The exact project hook definition does require user review and trust, so asking was procedurally understandable.
The root stopped at 03:47 Berlin after treating missing P1-04 source evidence as an owner blocker and P1-05 as sequenced behind P1-04.
The owner returned at 09:17 and corrected both assumptions, producing a preventable 5h29m51s stall.
Initial P1-04, P1-05, and architecture audits had already run concurrently; the failure was the transition from preview to execution, not a total absence of early parallel work.
The common-runtime writer began at 11:27 Berlin and the loop was still active 10h54m later at the cutoff.
The frozen common tip contained 18 commits across 20 files with +6,121/-5 lines.
Seventeen fresh implementation reviews all blocked; a sixteenth correction was in flight at cutoff.
Implementation writer plus reviewer roles consumed 230.1M tokens, 77.4% of subagent tokens.
Neither P1-04 nor P1-05 task record reached Complete, and neither task-specific implementation writer started.
Maximum concurrency was four with zero thread-limit errors.
Average concurrency while a subagent was active was 1.0767; only 5.23% of that time had two or more subagents active.
The corrected P1-04 and P1-05 evidence lanes overlapped after 09:20, proving the tasks had useful independent work.
The common gate later serialized both lanes, while the active common worktree and a dirty retained P1-10 worktree occupied the 2/2 writable-worktree budget.
All five root compactions received the validated SessionStart compact-hook injection.
Recovery took 33m41s total, 4.13% of pause-adjusted session time; median recovery was 7m16s.
Median context use at the first resumed coordination action was 57.97%.
The 22:00 Berlin recovery resumed at 64.60% context after 8m15s, 40 custom tool calls, 25 distinct normalized document/script paths, and 559,510 JSON characters of tool output.
The hook injection itself was only 6,043 characters. Most of the burden came from mandatory full rereads, duplicated chunked reads, and unrelated historical task material.
At the frozen cutoff preview.md was 67,073 bytes, 663 lines, and 17 top-level sections.
It received 22 patch events with 667 observed added lines and only 21 deleted lines.
The capsule received 79 patch events and 77 observed seal invocations despite durability-barrier guidance.
The preview therefore served simultaneously as design tree, current graph, decision log, and recovery narrative instead of a compact current-state index.
Of 45 heavy-admission samples, 13 were denied below 1.10 GiB and 32 were admitted.
The minimum admitted reading was 1.11 GiB and the maximum denied reading was 1.09 GiB, showing deterministic enforcement rather than an outcome-derived boundary.
Thirteen admitted samples were below the 1.50 GiB warning line.
Only one completed denial can be tied to ready heavy work; it cleared after 55 seconds. An open denial at cutoff had lasted at least 183 seconds.
Sample-to-sample denial intervals include owner waits, review work, and post-job readings and must not be counted as throughput loss.
Architecture, specification review, and planning used 12 threads, 16 turns, 43.76M tokens, 2h17m worker time, and $29.20 in API list-price equivalent.
Architecture alone used two threads, three turns, 9.80M tokens, and $6.90 equivalent.
Holding tokens fixed, Astra would price the architecture cohort at $17.25, a $10.35 premium; actual token behavior is unknown.
Astra is the strongest available synthesis candidate, but official guidance says it may ask more clarifying questions and is especially sensitive to instructions and skills.
Use Astra/high for one architecture lead and keep a different Sol/xhigh specification reviewer; do not replace the root or the independent gate yet.

recommendations.title: Introduce hot and cold recovery paths
recommendations.detail: For a valid capsule whose instruction-packet hash and active-contract SHA match, use one compact recovery-snapshot helper plus the active lane contract. Re-read the full skill, AGENTS files, preview, task set, and ADR chain only for corrupt state, changed instructions, material re-freeze, or uncertain ownership.

recommendations.title: Make preview.md a replace-in-place current graph
recommendations.detail: Cap it around 8–12 KiB, link exact tracked contracts, and move review/event history to a separate evidence stream. A recovery artifact should not become a shadow transcript.

recommendations.title: Split common runtime into acceptance milestones
recommendations.detail: Freeze and review bundle/canonical selection, coordinator state, persistence/replay, and health/receipts separately. Allow task-specific lanes to start as soon as their required milestone is accepted.

recommendations.title: Clean stale writable worktrees at intake
recommendations.detail: Recover, publish, or explicitly reserve dirty predecessor work before freezing the new graph. A retained dirty worktree should not silently consume half of the next run's writer capacity.

recommendations.title: Retain bounded correction continuity
recommendations.detail: Keep one writer for a bounded correction loop and optionally one reviewer for an incremental follow-up; use a fresh independent reviewer for milestone acceptance. The current all-fresh loop discarded context 17 times.

recommendations.title: Pilot Astra/high only for architecture
recommendations.detail: Measure first-pass specification acceptance, later review rounds, wall time, tokens, and list-price equivalent against Sol/xhigh. Preserve a different Sol/xhigh reviewer to protect independence.

recommendations.title: Replace the fixed memory floor with outcome calibration
recommendations.detail: Keep 1.10 GiB provisionally, but log operation family, start/min/post memory, duration, exit/outcome, paging or OOM symptoms, and queue delay. Lower in 0.10 GiB steps only when a meaningful sample shows clean outcomes; never infer delay from sparse sample gaps.

recommendations.title: Turn hook trust into positive startup evidence
recommendations.detail: Use a trusted UserPromptSubmit hook to inject the current hook-definition hash when orchestration is invoked, or include trust confirmation in the kickoff. If the definition changes or is untrusted, the marker disappears and the root asks.
